newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dresdner Asian unit's 1996 net up 72 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner Asian unit's 1996 net up 72 pct.

text.p: Dresdner (Southeast Asia) Ltd, a subsidiary of Dresdner Bank AG, said on Friday its 1996 net profit rose 72 percent to Singapore $38 million, marking its best performance ever.
It said in a statement that due to the strong results its authorised and paid-up share capital would be increased by S$25 million to S$100 million by means of a bonus issue.

The bank will also pay an ordinary dividend of 20 percent on its ordinary share capital of S$75 million, transfer S$20 million to its contingency reserve and carry forward S$8.4 million as retained profits, bringing total capital funds to S$272.9 million, it said.
Total assets grew 8.0 percent to S$4 billion, reflecting greater activity in interbank money market transactions and the loan business, the statement said.
It also announced the appointment of Gerd Hausler as chairman with effect from January 1, 1997, following the retirement of Meinhard Carstensen, who has resigned from the board of Dresdner Bank AG.
